scope.definition: The 26 modified and 177 newly created bootstrap README files in this checkout; excludes later review-directory README files and untouched documentation.

method: Processed frozen README files sequentially. Read their contents and resolved current local source references, with mirrored vendor contracts mapped to the unchanged upstream source tree.

The checker loads full document/cited-source text. It screens lexical source names and components of qualified symbols, relative Markdown links/heading targets and source hashes. These are mechanical checks rather than semantic proof or symbol ownership/type checking.

Compared behavior, limits, side effects, entry points, protocol boundaries and current implementation using focused semantic source reads. Reviewed composed contracts at their stated abstraction; a private helper without its own citation is not automatically missing functionality.

Compared all six worker.proto copies byte-for-byte; compared four embedded JSON error catalogs and decoded TypeScript/Python generated catalog entries. Screened committed Python/Go bindings for 71 distinct declared field names and ten RPC names, decoding the Python serialized descriptor before checking.
Checked 194 Cargo package/test references against local manifests; these are static target membership checks.

Read current authoring availability validation, Studio language selector, canonical/generated OpenAPI description, Java runner channels, Java packaging/release workflow and C# report retry loop to substantiate each reported discrepancy.
No subagents or external services were used. No runtime suites, builds, containers, publications, dependency installations, generated-file blessing or canonical task edits were performed.
limits: This is static drift detection, not an exhaustive semantic verification of every implementation body, field, race, dependency, transitive document or security guarantee.

Full-file loading by the checker must not be read as a claim that every source line received manual reasoning. Named interfaces/reference grounding was screened across all 203 targets; semantic reads were focused on documented behaviors and likely mismatches.
Example code blocks were not compiled or executed. Link checks do not verify remote URLs or renderer-specific line anchors.
Shared-contract byte equality and field/RPC-name screening do not establish generated-code byte equality, wire compatibility at runtime or a complete model/type equivalence proof.
Historical runtime/advisory notes were retained as historical claims; they were not reproduced or refreshed. No remote tag, release, registry or CI success was verified.
Existing dormant/nesting/capacity limitations were not treated as missing implementation when the README already states them; documented performance ceilings remain unaccepted.
The OpenAPI language-availability discrepancy is a linked local-contract finding supporting the root-guide issue. The API README itself is not falsely marked as contradicting its generated source.
